patterns: how do you introduce two people
entries.answer: An introduction is the moment two people are connected, and English words three separate things separately: being named to each other, being named to a room, and being left to do it yourself. The first is a courtesy from the person already present and it comes with a small script, being this is and introducing. The second is a social skill of its own. The third is where most people freeze, because there is nobody left to hand the floor to.

patterns: what to say to someone new
entries.answer: An icebreaker is a sentence used to open a conversation with a stranger, and the word assumes a room of people who do not know each other. A good one asks something easy to answer and hard to answer badly, which is exactly why the weather works and income does not. The worst are questions with a correct answer, because they end in agreement and leave nothing to follow. Asking something already answered a minute ago is the other failure.

patterns: is rapport the same as liking
entries.answer: Rapport is the easy mutual comfort that lets a conversation continue without effort, and it is not the same as liking somebody, which can exist without it. It is built from small agreements and matched pace, so two people who speak at the same speed and disagree about nothing yet find they are getting on well. Rapport can be built in a minute and lost in one, and it is usually lost by contradicting somebody in public or by making a joke at their expense.

patterns: how long does a first impression last
is warmth more important than competence
entries.answer: A first impression is the judgement formed in the first few seconds, and the research on it is unusually consistent: people form one almost immediately and revise it far less than they believe they will. What drives it is warmth before competence, so being liked counts for more than being right. The awkward consequence is that the impression is about manner rather than substance, and someone whose point was excellent can leave thinking they were not taken seriously.

entries.answer: Eye contact is the mutual meeting of gazes, and its meaning is entirely cultural even though the gesture itself is universal. Across much of Europe and North America a sustained look signals honesty and avoiding it signals evasion. Through much of Asia and in parts of the Middle East the convention reverses, and prolonged direct looking is read as disrespect or aggression. Somebody managing a conversation across that gap has to learn the other rule consciously.

patterns: is a gesture a form of communication
entries.answer: A gesture is a movement that carries meaning, and the word covers both the deliberate signals people make and the involuntary ones they cannot help. English adds a social layer of its own, because a movement can be fine among friends and inappropriate at work, and the same gesture reads differently in each place. The real difficulty is that the meaning is learned rather than universal, so people travel into a culture already following rules they have never been told.
